title: `<cmd> all <args>` gives the arguments to every option, so `check all --files x` fails at the four check options that take none
body:
Filed by dc for devbin 0.1.34, on vc's word. A course attendee reported it through agentic-engineering. Line numbers are at a329547f.

## What happens

`bin/devbin check all --files <file>` gives `--files <file>` to every check option. Only `check critic` takes arguments. `check format`, `check toolchain`, `check autotests` and `check targetdir` each stop with "check <option> takes no arguments" (lib/cmd/check:209, 371, 595 and 758). So `check all` ends FAILED and names those four, though nothing is wrong with the project. There is no way to scope `check all` to some files.

The failure is loud, so it is not a false green. It is a red with no cause in the project.

## Why

`run_all` (lib/resolve:1231) gives every option the same arguments (`run_option "$cmd" "$opt" "$@"`, :1303). No option says whether it takes arguments, so `all` cannot know which options the arguments are for. A refusal of all arguments in `all` is wrong too: `clean all --dry-run` passes its flags to each option on purpose.

Two built-in options take no arguments and drop them without a word: `docs agents` and `fmt swift`.

## Fix

1. Each built-in option declares whether it takes arguments, beside `builtin_option_in_all` (lib/builtins:449). The options that take none: check's format, toolchain, autotests and targetdir, `docs agents` and `fmt swift`.
2. A project's own option takes arguments by default, as now. A config key, `commands.<cmd>.options.<opt>.takes_args: false`, declares that it takes none. One resolver reads it, with the built-in's declaration as its default, as `option_in_all` reads `in_all`.
3. `run_all`, given arguments, refuses before any option runs when an option it would run takes none. It refuses with exit 1, and it writes no seal and no ledger. The refusal names each such option and points to `<cmd> <option> <args>`. devbin's wrapper flags (`--purge`, `--purge-only` and `--allow-empty`) are not arguments for this test. `all` never runs some options with the arguments and others without them.

## Proof

Localised arms, each red at a329547f:
- `check all --files x` refuses before any option runs: exit 1, no seal, and the message names format, toolchain, autotests and targetdir.
- `check critic --files x` still receives the arguments.
- `clean all --dry-run` still works.
- A project's run: option receives the arguments under `all` by default. With `takes_args: false` it is named in the refusal.
- A wrapper flag alone on `check all` does not trip the refusal.

## Resolution

Fixed in the devbin 0.1.34 batch, in two units, landed on main by fast-forward from a329547f: d1b1b831199447ef9c844d2c10c3cc4a38afd36e (If738d64) and d682f4847f01246f4d8ebe3eee75f46ae9b26594 (If738d64-2).

Unit If738d64: each built-in option declares whether it takes arguments, in _DEVBIN_BUILTIN_TAKES_NO_ARGS beside _DEVBIN_BUILTIN_NOT_IN_ALL. Six take none: check format, toolchain, autotests and targetdir, docs agents and fmt swift. A project's own option takes arguments by default, and commands.<cmd>.options.<opt>.takes_args: false declares that it takes none. The default comes from the built-in, as in_all's does, so a project's own run: line over a built-in option keeps it. Given arguments, run_all refuses with exit 1 before any option runs and before the seal ledger is made, when an option it would run takes none. The refusal names each such option and each that takes arguments, points to `<cmd> <option> <args>`, and names the takes_args key. devbin's wrapper flags are not arguments here, and all with no arguments runs as before.

Unit If738d64-2: named directly, docs agents and fmt swift refuse arguments as check format does, where they dropped them unread.

Proof on the Desk:
- Run 1, slot 01M8B7D1F88RZXPZACH3YZ0NDC, 2026-11-26 06:07Z to 06:10Z, at d6ce6377, unit 1 before its last line: at a329547f the check all arm, the project option arm and builtins' side-table arm were red, and the wrapper-flag and clean all --dry-run arms were green, as they are by construction. At the tip the 4 dispatch arms, the side-table arm, 3 config arms, 9 documentation arms and buildfmt's 2 no-arguments arms were green, and check lint read 0 breaches.
- Run 2, slot 01M8B7Q0XEKNGMC3D0HD8JYMT3, 2026-11-26 06:12Z to 06:16Z, at d682f484: at a329547f the check all arm, the project option arm and both If738d64-2 arms were red, and the 2 guard arms green. At the tip the 4 dispatch arms, docs.bats whole (6) and buildfmt's 10 swift and refuses-arguments arms were green, and check lint read 0 breaches.
